title: cost: autotune defaults for batching/caching and quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: set safer defaults and expose autotune knobs so customers get predictable unit economics out of the box. This PR combines three workstreams: 1) runtime defaults for batching and KV-prefetch caching to reduce per-token cost while retaining latency SLOs; 2) curated quantization profiles for common model families to enable faster trialing of lower-precision variants; 3) a small unit-economics (uecon) toolkit for estimating cost/latency tradeoffs from observed traces. Changes are conservative (defaults can be overridden) and accompanied by measurement harnesses and docs. Checklist: - [x] implement runtime defaults + feature flags - [x] add quant_profiles.yaml and selection logic - [x] add uecon CLI and API helpers - [x] add unit/integration tests - [x] update docs/ops and console tooling - [x] performance verification on perf-canary Summary of changes: - runtime: introduce AutotuneDefaults (batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, kv_prefetch_ratio) and a feature-flagged rollout; defaults are chosen from perf-canary traces to hit ~95th percentile latency SLOs while maximizing batching. - quant: add curated quant_profiles.yaml with profiles for gpt-small/med/large families and guidance for fp16/int8/ggml-quant variants; runtime will pick compatible profile when model metadata matches. - tooling: add tools/uecon/estimate_cost.py and a lightweight CLI (redwood uecon estimate) that consumes trace samples and returns delta-per-token, expected throughput, and suggested quant/profile combos. - docs: docs/ops/autotune.md with rollout instructions and how to interpret uecon output. CI and perf: added perf-canary job that runs synthetic traces against the new defaults; results included. Related: Linear ENG-4123 (autotune defaults), ENG-4187 (uecon tooling). Links: internal perf-canary dashboard (kanary/perf/74321), design doc (linear/ENG-4123/design). Testing: unit tests for quant profile selection and uecon estimator; integration test that validates end-to-end on a saved perf trace. Note: this PR is intentionally additive and gated behind feature flags; default rollout starts as opt-in for 2 weeks and then will be enabled for low-risk customers by percentage rollout.

review_comments: Ethan Ross: Can you clarify how kv_prefetch_ratio interacts with existing prefix cache settings? We saw increased memory use in a canary run.

Maya Patel: kv_prefetch_ratio is a heuristic multiplier applied to recent prefix hit rates; it's capped to a global memory budget and falls back to existing cache eviction behavior when budget reached. Added comments and tests.
Li Wei: Tests look good; request small refactor to dispatcher to avoid injecting defaults into legacy code paths.
Maya Patel: Refactored dispatcher to use an explicit AutotuneContext; moved legacy code path validation into compatibility layer. PTAL.
Carlos Mendoza: Approve after CI green and perf-canary shows no regressions at p50/p95.
CI: perf-canary job initially flagged a small p95 regression for long-tail seq=4096 traces; tuned batch_window_ms from 12->8ms to recover. Reran metrics; pass.
release_notes: Set conservative autotune defaults for batching/caching to reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs; add curated quantization profiles for common model families; include a unit-economics CLI/tool to estimate cost/latency tradeoffs from traces; gated rollout behind feature flags; no breaking changes.
summary_metrics: canary_after: ~18% reduction in cost-per-effective-token for conversational workloads at target SLO
